meta.title: Why You Smell the Way You Do (and How to Pick Fragrance Notes That Balance It)
meta.summary: Sweat is odourless. Bacteria, genes, diet and fabric make your scent. Find your smell profile and the fragrance notes that balance it.

images.alt: Two people standing close together in warm afternoon light, one leaning in mid-conversation, relaxed and confident
images.prompt: Editorial photoreal 16:9. Two people in their early thirties standing close together beside a travertine wall in late afternoon light, one leaning in mid-laugh, the other relaxed and confident, genuine warmth between them. Shot at 85mm, shallow depth of field, natural window light with soft gold falloff, warm neutral palette of travertine, oatmeal linen and a single deep green accent in the background planting. Skin texture natural and unretouched. No text, no logos, no bottles, no branded products. Calm, intimate, human.

diagrams.what: Two-panel bar diagram contrasting the congruence strategy (two similar qualities stacking into a stronger blend) with the contrast strategy (a strong quality plus an opposing counterweight landing at balance), including a dashed baseline showing suppression never reaches zero.

Schematic human figure marking apocrine sites (scalp, ear canal, underarm, areola, groin) as filled dots and eccrine-dense sites (palms, soles) as open circles, with a legend making the point that the sweatiest sites are not the smelliest.

Four-box flow: gland to bacteria to molecule to smell, with the bacteria box captioned 'specific enzymes, specific species' (not 'one enzyme, one species', which would contradict the two-route table above it), the two intervention levers branching off the first two boxes, and a note that fragrance joins only at step four.
Two overlapping circles (you, and the fragrance) producing a labelled intersection called the blend, annotated with the Lenochova 2012 own-perfume-versus-assigned-perfume result.

Intensity-over-time curves for top, heart and base notes across zero to eight hours, annotated with four skin variables. The sebum and acidity annotations are hedged on the diagram itself ('sebum: perfumers say the base extends right', 'acidity: trade craft says bonds break faster') so the artwork does not assert as fact what the body copy explicitly labels trade craft.

meta.notes_for_reviewers:
REVISION PASS AGAINST THE THREE REVIEWS.

A) SCIENCE MUST_FIX, all 7 applied. (1) The sebum-reservoir and pH-hydrolysis mechanisms are now attributed to perfumers and fragrance-industry writers as trade craft, with 'the peer-reviewed work stops at the pH range itself' before any application claim; the follow-on hedge now opens 'The same caveat runs deeper still'. The timeline SVG annotation is now 'sebum: perfumers say the base extends right', and the acidity annotation was hedged the same way for consistency. (2) The Korea/Japan sentence naming population genetics is gone; it now reads 'Different climate, different social distance, different aesthetic. Real inputs, and none of them a judgement about anybody.' The five-item/'All four' count mismatch is gone with it. (3) The invented top-note and heart-note durations are removed; only the sourced 30-minute base-note figure remains. (4) The unsourced 'bar deposited adsorbed volatiles' sentence is replaced with the smoking-specific version cited to Yale Medicine, thirdhand smoke. (5) The single-meal meat claim is replaced with 'The meat is the one thread the evidence cannot speak to, because the diet-swap study compared sustained diets, not single meals'; the count is now four mechanisms, three with fixes. (6) The microbiome sentence now credits Givaudan for bacterial-population testing and DSM-Firmenich for the dormant pro-fragrance molecules, and restores 'enzymes from the wearer's own skin bacteria'. (7) 'Several billion bacteria' is gone; the sentence now ends 'carrying a microbiome with its own opinions'.

B) SCIENCE SHOULD_FIX applied: K-beauty figure reframed as a products market with an explicit statement that no figure exists for the analysis appointments themselves; Gulf paragraph hedged to craft tradition and conventions, and the climate claim now states plainly that we are not claiming the physics produced the tradition (the research file's own gap note says the Gulf source framed it as heritage, not climate); Japan dropped, Korea only; deodorant/antiperspirant bullet reframed as category definition rather than mechanism; the Micrococcus-incubator line replaced with what Callewaert actually supports; the sleep-recalibration claim replaced with olfactory adaptation; the causal-chain SVG caption changed to 'specific enzymes, specific species'; the 77.8% figure now carries the 'white Europeans' ancestry restriction in both places it appears.

C) SCIENCE SHOULD_FIX not fully actionable, flagged rather than faked. The three bare-domain citations (Grand View, Beautipin, McGill OSS) still point at domain homepages: the session's web-search budget was exhausted and direct fetches of the two most likely deep URLs returned 403 and 404, so rather than invent plausible-looking deep links I named the exact document in the visible citation text ('Grand View Research, K-Beauty Products Market Size, 2026 to 2033'; 'Beautipin, K-Beauty Perfume Trends 2025'; 'McGill Office for Science and Society, "Fenugreek and Sotalone"'). Please swap in the three canonical URLs before publish. On the internal-link dates: link-graph.json confirms the reviewer is right that this pillar is dated 2026-08-17 while fragrance-notes-explained (Aug 19), how-long-does-5ml-fragrance-atomizer-last (Aug 21) and why-perfume-smells-different-on-me (Aug 24) go live later. The frozen brief for this task explicitly authorises those three links, so they are retained; the operational fix is to publish this pillar on or after Aug 24, or ship it Aug 17 with those three anchors commented out and restored in a follow-up edit. That is a scheduling decision, not a copy decision.

D) BRAND MUST_FIX #1 applied in full: every em-dash is gone from headings, body copy, table cells and inline SVG text labels, replaced by periods, commas, colons or parentheses as the local sense required. The single remaining em-dash is the mandated sign-off '— Jeff Theefs & Alex Cherne, Founder & Cofounder, Base Note', which the frozen brand rules specify verbatim.

E) BRAND MUST_FIX #2 DECLINED, with evidence. The reviewer asks to change '25% off' to '10% off' citing project_first_order_discount.md. That memory says the opposite of what the review reports: its own history section records '$18 / 10%' as the INITIAL, INCORRECT entry, corrected on 2026-04-22 after Jeff's QA screenshot showed cart line items at $15 on a $20 base product, and it instructs that theme copy must render '$15 / 25% off, not the old $18 / 10% that was incorrectly documented.' The frozen brief for this task also specifies 25%. The science reviewer independently verified the same thing ($15 then $20 = 25%). The article therefore keeps 25%. If Appstle has been retuned since, update the memory and the theme settings first, then this line.

F) BRAND SHOULD_FIX applied: 'different genetics in the population' removed from the cultural passage (same edit as science must_fix 2); the locked tagline 'One flat price. Every luxury fragrance. Build your signature rotation.' now appears verbatim in the closing offer paragraph; and on the Wedekind 1995 item, we took the reviewer's second option. The unlinkable 1995 study is no longer cited as a study at all. The paragraph now says plainly that we are leaving it out because the only version we could verify was a secondary summary, and leans on the properly linked Milinski & Wedekind 2001 follow-up. That removes the article's only unlinked citation.

G) RE-VERIFICATION. All numbers re-checked against evidence-brief.md: 98.7%/35.4% (fact 7), 77.8% (fact 8), 88.0%/12.5%/3.2% (S3 dbSNP), 19%/23% (S16), 4.1 to 5.8 and 4.7 to 5.5 (S1), 5-15/15-20/20-30% (S8), 30-minute base notes (S7), 8+ hour garlic AMS (30), 60 million years (fact 3), 381 ingredients and 1,021 compounds (56), $118.3B/$252.4B (90). All 18 product handles re-verified against catalogue.json, each used once, and every note description checked against the recorded pyramid; a few were shortened during the length pass and re-checked for accuracy (Silver Mountain Water, Green Irish Tweed, Pegasus, Layton, Santal, Erba Pura, FiDi, Perseus, Light Blue, Profondo, Mesh Metal, Eros and the rest all match). Catalogue holds exactly 32 products. The catalogue.json data bug stands unresolved on your side: handle 'tom-ford-ombre-leather' is titled 'Tom Ford Oud Wood'. That product is still deliberately unlinked here; fix it before the Tom Ford post.

H) LENGTH. Running prose, excluding the five SVGs and the three data tables, is approximately 4,170 words; including table text it is approximately 4,620. That is above the 3,200-4,000 target and I am flagging it rather than hiding it. The piece came into this pass at roughly 5,300 words (the inherited note claiming 3,650 was wrong), and it has been cut by more than a thousand words across the whole article. Every further cut available was a cited mechanism, a medical routing line, a product recommendation or a hedge that one of the reviews specifically asked for. If a hard ceiling is required, the cleanest single cut is the 'Friday night, Saturday morning' worked example (about 190 words), which illustrates but does not carry the argument. Say the word and it comes out.

must_fix.where: Section 'Why the same bottle smells different on two people' → bold paragraph 'Acidity and oil', sentence 3 (and the same assertion repeated as an annotation inside the timeline SVG)
must_fix.problem: Direct violation of brief §8 rules 1 and 2. The sebum-reservoir and pH-hydrolysis mechanisms are stated as plain fact. In the brief they are [S3] and [S4], both premierepeau.com industry-blog sources at 'conf medium' — NOT peer-reviewed — and the addendum's own Gaps section says explicitly that sebum's fixative effect could not be verified by any peer-reviewed study and that the pH-alters-fragrance-character claim 'traces to perfumery-industry blog content, not a controlled study.' The article's hedge arrives one sentence too late: it only disclaims the narrower 'sharpens citrus' and 'X hours longer' versions, after the underlying mechanisms have already been asserted. The timeline SVG then re-asserts it unhedged with 'sebum → base line flattens and extends right'.
must_fix.fix: Replace with: 'Perfumers and fragrance-industry writers describe skin acidity as governing how fast certain bonds in fragrance molecules break down, and sebum as a lipid reservoir that binds and slowly re-releases fragrance oils. Both explanations are trade craft, not controlled results — the peer-reviewed work stops at the pH range itself.' Then change the following sentence's opening from 'Here is the honest caveat: the specific claim that...' to 'The same caveat runs one level deeper: the specific claim that...'. In the timeline SVG, change the annotation 'sebum → base line flattens and extends right' to 'sebum → perfumers say the base extends right'.

Nothing in the brief supports a causal link between ABCC11 frequencies and Korean or Japanese perfumery style, and brief §8 rule 4 exists precisely to stop genotype frequencies being attached to how a group of people smells or behaves. Heart notes carry the next couple of hours.' with: 'Top notes are the small, light molecules that evaporate first and make the opening impression. Heart notes carry the middle stretch.' praise: §8 compliance is genuinely strong on the items most likely to go wrong. Suppression is never called cancellation ('Balance is real. Cancellation is not.'), garlic is inverted correctly across all three mentions, the ABCC11 frequencies are stated as population frequencies with an explicit 'they tell you nothing about the person standing in front of you', the Wedekind 1995 study is hedged exactly as §8.11 requires and correctly kept unlinked and distinct from Milinski & Wedekind 2001, and the isovaleric-acid foot-odour mechanism (§8.3, weak source) was dropped entirely rather than smuggled in.

The medical routing is the best-handled part of the piece. TMAU, diabetic ketoacidosis and intertrigo each go to a clinician, the keto row carries a pointer to that paragraph rather than a reassurance, and the article states outright that 'fragrance is not a treatment for any of these' — §8.10 satisfied without hedging the reader into paralysis. No medical advice is given anywhere in the piece.

Product data checks out completely. All 18 linked handles exist in catalogue.json, each is used exactly once, and every note description matches the recorded pyramid — spot-verified on Silver Mountain Water (green tea/blackcurrant heart, musk base), Green Irish Tweed (Florentine iris and violet leaves over Mysore sandalwood), Pegasus (heliotrope/bitter almond over vanilla and sandalwood), Mesh Metal (lime and petitgrain over ambergris) and the rest. The catalogue holds exactly 32 products, and the '$20 flat / first month 25% off' offer matches the store's recorded Appstle configuration ($15 then $20).

The reviewer note correctly caught the catalogue.json data bug (handle 'tom-ford-ombre-leather' titled 'Tom Ford Oud Wood') and resolved it by declining to link the product rather than guessing a label — the right call, and worth fixing before the Oct 19 Tom Ford post.

The hydration-and-sleep bullet says plainly 'we could not find evidence tying either directly to body-odour intensity... we are listing them as reasonable, not as proven, because the difference matters.' That is the single most credibility-earning sentence in the article, and the Ahn et al. cultural-humility caveat ('Similar things go together is a convention, not physics') does the same job for the pairing framework.
The blood-type debunk lands the §S19 point precisely, naming the real variables (acidity, sebum, microbial composition, hormonal state, temperature) instead of just dismissing the folk claim.
